notes.title: Playtest Version 1.0
notes.notes: After months of optimization and a suite of changes and adjustments, a real playable version of the game is finally ready to be tested. Many, many bugs still remain that I can't find on my own!

notes.title: Playtest v0.03
notes.notes:
[b]Fixes[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed radio system breaking when any player detached their radio.
[*] Fixed keybinds not actually working or saving.
[*] Fixed a few issues with the radio being usable when it shouldn't've been.
[*] Fixed issue where when a player died and dropped their items, anything that wasn't currently in their hand was invisible.
[*] Fixed issue that when you were holding something and picked up a ragdoll, the thing would stay visible.
[*] Fixed issue where you could hear players igniting and burning across the world.
[*] Fixed issue where scrolling quickly while moving could leave the hold position of objects at weird spots.
[*] Reduced ethereal radiation levels.
[*] Removed bunnyhopping. Sorry. I don't want the default behavior of players to be required to be constantly jumping everywhere at all times.
[*] Removed the murderspheres at the back of the ship that were used for death and ragdoll debugging.[/list]

[b]Additions[/b]
[list]
[*] Added player steam name indicator when hovering cursor over a player.
[*] Added indicator above player head to show their voice activity to better help identify players in a crowded room.
[*] Added number key support for inventory selection.
[/list]

[b]Known Issues[/b]
Tons, but two major ones:
[list]
[*] You can join someone's game late, but the game will break for everyone. 
[*] Players seem to need to sit in the lobby for a few seconds before the host hits Start Game, or they don't get pulled into the game.
[*] Minor: The right side window has no collision. This is for debugging and I forget to turn collision back on.
[/list]

notes.title: First Playtest Complete!
notes.notes:
This evening I completed the first every playtest of the game with myself and some friends. There had been previous tests to try out basic features on their own, but today was the actual first test with core gameplay mechanics in place and a relative lack of game-breaking issues. As expected there were some bugs, some worse than others, but these will be fixed up in the coming days and the game will be trialed once again to keep trying to find more.

I've been working on this project almost every day for the past 13 months, and in that time I've made essentially zero community-building effort, with all my game-focused time going toward making the game, but that's going to need to change in the coming weeks and months now that I actually have a basic playable product that people have access to.

For now, no more playtesters will be let in yet. I want to iron out game-breaking bugs, after which I'll add in more game variety which is currently turned off for testing to only cover the core gameplay elements, after which the game will need MORE testing. After THAT point, once there aren't severe issues, I'll start letting in more testers. I want the playtest experience to be the game itself, I don't want part of the experience to be knowing what not to do because it breaks the game. You should be able to just play it.

In the meantime, feel free to join the discord server linked on the game's steam page to chat with me about the game or anything.
